**Trustly raises new capital to fund AI platform after deep restructuring**

*Weeks after cutting a quarter of its workforce, a capital raise will fund a real-time intelligence layer across the Swedish open banking payments firm's network.*

Trustly has secured new capital to fund what it describes as a shift from pure payment processing toward a real-time intelligence platform. The investment will support expansion of its open banking payments network, which currently spans the US, Canada and Europe.

The fundraise comes barely two weeks after Trustly cut roughly 25% of its staff in a push toward profitability, a move that signalled the company was under pressure to demonstrate a sustainable business model. Neither Trustly nor its investors have publicly explained the relationship between the restructuring and the fundraise, though the proximity of the two events suggests the cuts were at minimum a precondition for new investment.

The pivot toward intelligence and data services layered on top of payment flows mirrors a broader pattern among open banking infrastructure providers seeking to extract more value from their networks. Trustly must retain merchant and bank relationships through significant organisational disruption for the strategy to succeed, and the company's ability to do so while simultaneously building out a new platform will test its operational capacity.

*Sources: [Trustly Raises New Capital to Power the Next Era in Open Banking](https://finovate.com/trustly-raises-new-capital-to-power-the-next-era-in-open-banking/) — Finovate*

**ANZ completes live cross-border payment on Swift's shared ledger**

*The transaction marks another production milestone for the shared ledger infrastructure, following BNP Paribas and HSBC's corporate payment in September.*

ANZ has completed a live corporate treasury transaction using tokenised deposits settled on Swift's blockchain-based shared ledger. The cross-border payment is the latest in a series of production transactions on the platform, which moved from pilot to live use in July.

Swift's shared ledger has been progressing through increasingly significant milestones. Banks piloted live transactions in July, BNP Paribas and HSBC completed the first corporate payment in September, and ACI Worldwide connected its cloud payments hub to the platform the same month. ANZ's transaction extends the network's geographic reach into the Asia-Pacific region and adds another major bank to the roster of active participants.

The steady drumbeat of live transactions signals that tokenised settlement infrastructure is moving past proof-of-concept. Banks now face a practical challenge: how quickly they will route meaningful volumes through it, and what that means for existing correspondent banking arrangements.

*Sources: [ANZ completes cross-border tokenised deposit payment with Swift ledger](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48534/anz-completes-cross-border-tokenised-deposit-payment-with-swift-ledger?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**Basware acquires payment fraud prevention platform Trustpair**

*Growing corporate demand for fraud prevention at the point of payment initiation is driving consolidation in the B2B payment integrity space, with pre-payment verification now being embedded directly into invoice processing workflows.*

Basware, the invoice lifecycle management company, has acquired Trustpair, a platform that verifies supplier bank account details before payments are released. Financial terms were not disclosed.

The acquisition sits at the intersection of two trends shaping European corporate payments. First, the SEPA instant payments regulation's payee verification requirements are pushing all payment initiators to validate recipient details in real time. Second, invoice fraud and business email compromise remain among the most costly forms of payment fraud for corporates, and prevention increasingly depends on automated checks embedded in existing workflows rather than bolt-on solutions.

By integrating Trustpair's verification capabilities into its invoice processing platform, Basware is betting that corporates want fraud prevention built into the accounts payable process itself rather than handled separately. Basware's core business is managing the full invoice lifecycle, so adding pre-payment verification is a logical extension that could also strengthen its position against competitors offering similar end-to-end propositions.

*Sources: [Basware buys payment fraud prevention platform Trustpair](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48532/basware-buys-payment-fraud-prevention-platform-trustpair?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**TrueLayer and SumUp partner on open banking account top-ups**

*Pay-by-bank functionality is being added to SumUp's personal account top-ups, extending open banking deeper into the SME payments stack.*

TrueLayer is partnering with SumUp to enable open banking-powered account top-ups for SumUp's personal account holders. The integration allows merchants using SumUp's financial services to fund their accounts directly from their bank, bypassing card rails.

SumUp has evolved from a card terminal provider into a broader financial services platform for small businesses, offering business accounts, invoicing and lending alongside its core payment acceptance product. Adding open banking top-ups through TrueLayer removes friction from a routine task, since merchants currently funding accounts via card or bank transfer face either interchange costs or slower settlement.

Open banking payments are finding traction in Europe not by competing head-on with cards at the checkout, but by gaining ground in adjacent workflows where cost savings or speed improvements are more immediately apparent to the end user, particularly in B2B and merchant services contexts.

*Sources: [TrueLayer and SumUp partner to simplify account top-ups](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/111129/truelayer-and-sumup-partner-to-simplify-account-top-ups) — Finextra Research*
